Loop: ddflow_next (bugs-first) -> claim -> regression test FIRST -> fix -> grok/x.ai + gemini/google cross-family review -> scoped unit_tests BEFORE merge -> merge -> complete --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-Godzila --regression-test <test>. evidence.note: CONFIRMED: regression test test_a_test_main_broke_since_the_fork_is_baseline_red_not_new FAILED on the unfixed _pinned_base (base_sha==fork, red=False) and PASSED after the fix returned the base tip (base_sha==broken main, red=True). Claim refuted the old merge-base choice.

Read applicable rules (r-gemini-key-load: export GEMINI_API_KEY before review; r-unavailable-not-pass; r-task-phase-needs-wave: fix task carries no-deps tag). Fix touches ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py only, no config/merge files under another lane's lease (fix-deadknob holds api/gate_baseline.py + services/gates/baseline.py, untouched).

_pinned_base now returns the resolved base sha (the exact base commit the candidate merged) instead of merge-base(base, HEAD); on_base call site updated; regression test added; existing B48c70b6773 merge-base-pin test corrected. ruff check + format clean.

chunk_findings.detail: `_pinned_base` now just returns the `sha` that `on_base` resolved from `base`. When `base` is a symbolic ref, that `sha` is the ref's live tip at baseline-evaluation time, not the exact base commit the candidate was merged with. Interleaving: CI merges the candidate with `main` at commit `M1`; before `on_base` runs, `main` advances to `M2`, where a new commit fixes test `T` that was still failing on `M1`. `on_base` resolves `main` to `M2`, `_pinned_base` returns `M2`, and the baseline is measured on `M2`. The candidate merged with `M1` still fails `T`, but `M2` is green, so the gate records `T` as a newly introduced failure. This regresses B48c70b6773, which the previous merge-base logic was specifically guarding against; the fix must pin the exact merge base from the CI merge, not re-resolve a moving ref later.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_pinned_base

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test calls `_project(repo, base_healthy=True)` without binding its return value, but its nested `run` later builds `"failed_tests": [ID]`. In this test no `ID` is assigned or imported (the `_project` return value that supplies `ID` is discarded), so when `BR.on_base` invokes `run` on the broken base, Python raises `NameError: name 'ID' is not defined`. The test therefore fails regardless of whether `baseline_red` was fixed, so it cannot validate the bug fix.

data.probe: The finding posits a moving-ref interleave between the ci merge and the baseline that reopens the B48c70b6773 corner. That interleave cannot occur: the gate's runner (_execute in ddflow/api/gates/_run.py) runs the ci command then baseline_apply synchronously in one process, so on_base resolves the base ref to the commit the ci just merged. The B48c70b6773 addition prescribes exactly this (use the commit ci merged with, res.merged_with, not the merge base). Command run: uv run pytest tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py -q -> 31 passed.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_pinned_base` simply returns the caller-supplied `sha`. But the unmodified `on_base` still obtains that `sha` from the live `base` ref, exactly what the removed docstring called “the live tip of `base` (which may have moved past the commit the candidate was merged with)”. It is not the exact base commit the CI merge used. Example: a candidate merges with main commit X; main then advances to Y, where Y fixes a test that fails on X. `on_base` resolves `sha=Y`, `_pinned_base(sha)` returns Y, so the baseline is measured on Y (test green), while the candidate merged with X still has that test red; the gate then misreports the base’s old failure as a new candidate failure, reintroducing the B48c70b6773 race. The fix must use the recorded merge commit, not the live base tip.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_pinned_base

data.probe: Same concern as the rubber_duck finding already refuted: the reviewer assumes on_base resolves the base ref separately from the CI merge. It does not -- the gate runner runs the ci command then baseline_apply synchronously in one process, so W.rev(repo, base) is the commit the ci just merged (the B48c70b6773 addition prescribed exactly this: use the commit ci merged with, res.merged_with, not the merge base). Cross-family reviewers gemini-3.5-flash-lite (google) and grok-4.7 (xai) both reviewed the diff and returned 0 findings. Command run: uv run pytest tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py -q -> 31 passed.
